clue.text: The height of disrepute? A result of sorts

indicators.note: something 'of sorts' is a rough version of itself, so these letters are only loosely the words given and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wry question: is a scandalous outcome the peak of shame?
explanation.walkthrough: 'of sorts' rearranges all sixteen letters of DISREPUTE A RESULT; the first 'of' just joins the definition to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressure altitude is an aviation term: the height above a standard datum plane, read from an altimeter set to standard pressure.

clue.text: See 27
Is dotted over back of head, shaken at sudden collars

parts.note: something over is finished, done

indicators.note: to collar is to grab round the neck, so the shaken letters wrap around the single letter
shaken letters are jumbled into a new order
the back of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A medical-sounding scene: something dotted over the back of the head, a shaken patient seized suddenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is dotted' is the definition, as in every i dotted: complete. 'shaken' turns AT SUDDEN into ANDUSTED, which 'collars' the D from 'back of head' to give AND DUSTED.
explanation.definitionFit: A job with every i dotted is finished in every detail, which is what the idiom for a completed task means.

clue.text: See 3
Selection of hors d'oevres not for women — their starters refused over sudden outburst

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the letters are turned to read upwards, from the bottom
the starters of the two words are their first letters, and refusing them drops them

parts.note: meze is a Mediterranean selection of small starters
for men only, that is men's

explanation.surface: A diner turns down a plate of starters because it is a men-only menu, then sneezes over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their' refers to both words just clued, so each loses its first letter; 'over', in a down clue, sends the remainder upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneeze is a sudden involuntary expulsion of air through the nose and mouth: an outburst in the most physical sense.

clue.text: With which one's driven to speak of liquor under orders

definitions.text: With which one's driven to speak

indicators.note: orders as a verb means arranges, so the letters of these words are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Drink loosens tongues: a man under the influence finds he cannot stop talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' looks like part of a phrase 'under orders', but it is fodder; 'orders' alone signals the rearrangement of OF LIQUOR UNDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Furor loquendi is Latin for a rage or mania for talking, the compulsion that drives one to speak.

clue.text: Romantic brother keeping some outside is menial worker in firm

indicators.note: a container keeps what is inside it, so the brother's letters hold the rest

parts.note: Fra is the title of an Italian friar or monk, a religious brother

indicators.note: the word for some goes outside the other letters

parts.note: some as in any at all

indicators.note: the earlier letters go in the firm's abbreviation

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
taken as written
a cog is an unimportant worker in a big machine or organisation

explanation.surface: A romantic monk shelters someone outside who works as a lowly hand in a company.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the containers from the inside out: the innermost pair sits in the firm, the word for some goes round that, and the brother holds everything, his last letter ending the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Goya, the Spanish painter, is counted among the founding figures of Romanticism in art.

clue.text: Unorthodox layouts in down clues for sure!

indicators.note: an unorthodox version departs from the standard, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A solver remarks on the setter's odd way of arranging down clues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clues' is a link word: the rearranged LAYOUTS IN DOWN clues, or signals, the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying you wouldn't refuse something is a British understatement for accepting gladly: yes please, certainly.

clue.text: Dawn assault captures chief island port

indicators.note: the phrase captures, holds within it, a run of its own letters

explanation.surface: A military raid at first light seizes the main harbour of an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Nassau is the capital and main port of the Bahamas, on New Providence island.

clue.text: Floor — middle one, bereft of walls

indicators.note: the walls of a word are its outermost letters, and being bereft of them strips both ends

parts.note: centre means middle and sole means one, so the phrase gives centre sole

explanation.surface: A building with a middle storey that has lost its walls.
explanation.walkthrough: Losing its walls means the joined phrase for middle one loses its outer letters, the first of the first word and the last of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: An entresol is a mezzanine, a low storey between the ground and first floors.

clue.text: The sound of Cliff? Hardly!

indicators.note: the sound of a word is how it is said, so a word that sounds the same as cliff's synonym is wanted

parts.note: a scar is a steep rocky cliff

explanation.surface: A wry comment that ska is not the music of Cliff Richard, the British pop singer.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent SCAR, a crag, is said like SKA. Ska is a sound, a style of music, but hardly Cliff Richard's, hence 'Hardly!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ska is a Jamaican music genre, a sound with offbeat rhythms quite unlike a clean-cut pop crooner's.

clue.text: Stew Northerners consume (but not with peelings of tatties)

indicators.note: the words say the following letters are to be left out

parts.note: the Scots live in the north of Britain

indicators.note: the peel of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: to use is to consume

explanation.surface: Scots eat a stew, but without peeled potatoes; tatties are Scottish for potatoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peelings of tatties' gives T and S, and 'but not with' removes them from SCOTS USE.
explanation.definitionFit: Scouse is a meat and vegetable stew from Liverpool, which also gave its name to Liverpudlians.

clue.text: Likely end? Criminal one to be suspended

definitions.text: Likely end? Criminal one to be suspended

indicators.note: criminal means bent or crooked, so the letters are twisted out of shape
being suspended means stood down, taken out, so this letter goes from the pool

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Asking how a notorious outlaw was likely to finish: hanged.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange LIKELY END after taking out I ('one to be suspended'). The whole clue is the definition too: Ned Kelly, the Australian bushranger, was hanged in 1880.
explanation.definitionFit: Ned Kelly was a notorious Australian outlaw executed by hanging, the likely end for a criminal of his day.

clue.text: Brynner and Kerr, perhaps close to bar, drink!

parts.note: Yul Brynner and Deborah Kerr starred in The King and I, so they are the K and the I

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, its final letter

explanation.surface: Two film stars, near the bar, call for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Kir is a French aperitif of white wine with blackcurrant liqueur, cassis.

clue.text: Make false accusations when blue

parts.note: as in 'as I left', meaning when
perse is a dark greyish blue

explanation.surface: Someone in a low mood lashes out with unfounded charges.
explanation.definitionFit: To asperse is to cast aspersions, to slander or spread damaging lies about someone.

clue.text: One drowned by river beginning to ascend

definitions.text: One drowned by river beginning to ascend

indicators.note: being drowned is going under, so in this down clue the letter for one sits below the river

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone swept under by a rising river.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a ria is a valley drowned by the sea, the river's mouth where the tide comes up.
explanation.definitionFit: A ria is a long narrow inlet formed when a river valley is submerged by rising sea levels.

clue.text: Thin beard and divine fringes

indicators.note: to fringe is to border, so the divining word sits around the bristle

parts.note: to scry is to divine the future, as with a crystal ball
an awn is the bristly beard on an ear of barley

explanation.surface: A gaunt holy man with a straggly beard.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrawny means lean and bony, unattractively thin.

clue.text: It may necessitate hand over mouth

definitions.text: It may necessitate hand over mouth

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece is placed above the second

parts.note: a hand is a round of applause, a clap
trap is slang for the mouth

explanation.surface: Some talk is so bad you'd want to stop the speaker's mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give him a hand' means applaud, so hand is CLAP; whole clue also defines: nonsense that calls for silencing the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is pretentious nonsense, the sort of empty talk one wishes someone would stop.

clue.text: See 1
See 22
In confusion, an end to Juliet, replacing him among the dead?

definitions.text: In confusion, an end to Juliet, replacing him among the dead?

indicators.note: the new letters take the place of the man's letter

parts.note: the morgue is where the dead are laid
with Juliet in the clue, him is Romeo, R in the radio alphabet

parts.words: In confusion, an end to Juliet
parts.note: an plus the end letter of Juliet, T, in confusion, that is jumbled

explanation.surface: Juliet's tragedy: amid the chaos she ends up among the dead, her lover gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In confusion' jumbles AN plus T to NTA, which replaces the R ('him', Romeo) in MORGUE. Romeo, a Montague, lies dead in the Capulet tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Montague is Romeo's family name in Shakespeare's play, so he is the dead lover the clue points at.

clue.text: Big shot sounded out when cycling

indicators.note: cycling letters moves some from one end of the word round to the other

parts.note: to let rip is to speak out loudly and freely

explanation.surface: A loud explosion heard while riding a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when cycling' takes the LE of LET RIP round to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A triple is a large measure of spirits, three shots in one glass.

clue.text: I say proceed to ring road north — be clear about it

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so the proceed letters go round

parts.note: go on means proceed

indicators.note: about means surrounding, and it refers back to north just named

parts.note: taken as written
nett means clear, after deductions, as in clear profit
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A driver is told to go round the ring road heading north and get clear of it.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'about it', the word it points back to north, the letter just named, which the clear word and be wrap round.
explanation.definitionFit: Gordon Bennett is a mild British exclamation of surprise, like 'I say!' or 'good grief'.

clue.text: I begin to repair halves for one 6 Down

indicators.note: re-pairing the two halves puts them back together the other way round

parts.note: to start is to begin

explanation.surface: A fresh start mending broken pieces, as a restorer of Goya might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repair' is read as re-pair: I START split as IST and ART and joined again in reverse order.
explanation.definitionFit: Goya was a painter, so an artist is what he is, with 'for one' saying he is an example.

clue.text: The best bet? Sleep

definitions.meaning: in racing tips, a ... is the tipster's most confident selection of the day

explanation.definitionFit: Nap is both a racing tipster's surest pick and a brief doze, two unrelated senses of one word.

clue.text: Particle, larger than normal, has it in for most common of neutrinos

indicators.note: the word for for has the following letters in it
the letters go in, inside the pro word

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
OS is the abbreviation for outsize
taken as written
N appears twice in neutrinos, more than any other letter

explanation.surface: A physics paper claims an outsized particle has it in for the commonest kind of neutrino.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most common of neutrinos' is its most frequent letter, N, rather than a first or last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A positron is the antimatter partner of the electron, a subatomic particle with positive charge.

clue.text: Hats off to young Saturngazers, fixing the variable moon

indicators.note: the outer letters fix, or hold firmly, the jumbled letters between them
the hats of words are their tops, their first letters
variable letters can be put into a varied order

explanation.surface: A salute to young astronomers who have pinned down a moon whose brightness changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hats off' looks like a salute but takes the first letters of 'to young Saturngazers'; 'variable' jumbles THE into ETH.
explanation.definitionFit: Tethys is one of the larger moons of Saturn, named after a Titaness of Greek myth.

clue.text: Show exhausted worker (miles logged) people reluctant to stir?

indicators.note: logged means recorded inside, so the letter goes into the words for the worker

parts.note: all out means exhausted
a hand is a worker, as a farmhand
people who will not rouse others or rise up are not rousers

explanation.surface: A shattered labourer, miles on the clock, among people who won't get moving.
explanation.walkthrough: The last piece splits NO TROUSERS as NOT ROUSERS, people who do not stir.
explanation.definitionFit: Being all mouth and no trousers is a British idiom for boasting with no substance behind it: all show.
